qolFindings.title: A phone that never used the backup and still holds an erased course brings that course back when it signs in. This is now intended (decision 19), not an accident.
qolFindings.evidence: src/persistence/syncMode.ts:311-321 records keep = 1 for every course copied at the switch. The first settle then lifts the server's erased_courses record and the course uploads. That covers DI-B6-R2-2 (the owner imported the course's file on a fresh phone). It also covers a second 0.4-mode phone that simply kept the old course: its first sign-in after the erase restores the course online, and the owner is not asked. docs/working/OWNER_DECISIONS.md 19 now says so explicitly ('signing in on a phone that holds it and never used the backup ... is accepted again'), so this is a recorded owner trade-off rather than a defect. It is worth confirming with the owner at the B6 or UG4 owner check.
qolFindings.reproduction: Code reading; the fake test 'signing in with a course whose id was erased elsewhere uploads it, accepted again' passes and shows the behaviour.
